title: Proper normal pair preparation over a radicial constant extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a nonempty separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Z\subseteq X$ a nowhere dense closed subset. There are a proper finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$, a dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a nowhere dense closed subset $C\subseteq\overline X$ with $C\cap X=Z$, a finite purely inseparable field extension $e/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], and a proper finite-type $e$-scheme $B$ with a projective surjective $k$-morphism $r:B\to\overline X$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The scheme $B$ is a finite disjoint union of nonempty integral normal schemes and is geometrically reduced over $e$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; geometrically reduced means that every extension of the base field gives a reduced scheme. The morphism $r$ gives a bijection between the generic points of the components of $B$ and those of $\overline X$, and each corresponding residue-field extension is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The subset $r^{-1}C$ is the support of an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. The extension $e/k$ is trivial in characteristic zero. Purely inseparable means that in characteristic $p>0$ every element has a $p$-power lying in the smaller field, and means equality in characteristic zero. Projective uses the projective-bundle convention. Empty $Z$ is allowed. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150 (compactification, reduced components, radicial constants, blowup, finite normalization), applied to the finitely many components with one common finite radicial constant extension. The compactification is chosen with C the closure of Z; including the complement of X is optional, not required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-marked-radicial-compactification] to $(X,Z)$. Obtain $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $C=\overline{j(Z)}$, $e/k$, and $t:T=(\overline X_e)_{\mathrm{red}}\to\overline X$. Thus $C\cap X=Z$, $t$ is finite radicial and a homeomorphism, and $T/e$ is proper and geometrically reduced; $e=k$ in characteristic zero.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150; assembly of returned proof steps 1--3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-component-cartier-blowup] to $(T,t^{-1}C)$. It provides the reduced components $T_i$, the proper surjective integral birational blowups $b_i:S_i\to T_i$, and effective Cartier ideals on $S_i$ supported on $b_i^{-1}(t^{-1}C\cap T_i)$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150; assembly of returned proof steps 4--6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-projective-birational-model] over $e$ to each proper integral $S_i$. Obtain $c_i:Y_i\to S_i$ and its finite normalization $n_i:N_i\to Y_i$, with $N_i$ normal integral and a closed immersion $N_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$. The composite to $S_i$ is proper, surjective and birational.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150; assembly of returned proof steps 7--8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-cartier-geometric-reduction] with $T_0=T_i$, $S=S_i$ and $h=c_i n_i$. Each $N_i/e$ is geometrically reduced, and the Cartier ideal on $S_i$ extends to an effective Cartier ideal on $N_i$ with support $(b_i c_i n_i)^{-1}(t^{-1}C\cap T_i)$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150; assembly of returned proof steps 9--10.

proof.text: The maps $q_i=b_i c_i n_i$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], surjective, and birational: intersect the dense open of $S_i$ where $c_i n_i$ is an isomorphism with $b_i^{-1}U_i$; its image under $b_i$ is a dense open of $T_i$ on which the composite is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-component-model-assembly] to them. It gives $B=\coprod_iN_i$, proper and H-projective over $e$, and $q:B\to T$, surjective with a bijection on component generic points and isomorphisms on their residue fields. Its Cartier ideal has support $q^{-1}t^{-1}C$. Set $r=tq$. Surjectivity composes, and the two bijections on component generic points compose. At a generic point the residue map of $q$ is an isomorphism, so the residue extension of $r$ is the finite purely inseparable extension of $t$. Its Cartier support is $q^{-1}t^{-1}C=r^{-1}C$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150; assembly of returned proof steps 11--12.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] to $e/k$, the projective $e$-scheme $B$, the separated $k$-scheme $\overline X$, and $r$. This makes $r$ projective in the required projective-bundle convention. The preceding constructions supply every other clause. If $Z$ is empty, each component blowup is the identity and all Cartier supports are empty.
